exact_statement: Determine how large n must be as a function of r >= 2 so that there is an antichain in 2^[n] occupying n-3 distinct ranks and containing at least r members on every occupied rank.
scope_notes: Round seven proves one literal critical-budget switch on actual K4,r9 odd j=1231 and classifies the inherited one-wall rank-two shifts s<=3.
This round asks whether the actual lattice q_(j+2)=4q_j-4 selects a stable positive cell or a controlled first wall for every odd j, or at least for an explicitly infinite subsequence.
The first obstruction is the higher-carry window: if q^- is the largest actual q below B_n, a rank-two one-wall description fails only when q^+ - B_n <= 20n-74, where q^+=4q^- -4.

An all-j K4,r9 recovery theorem is still local route progress, not the public antichain theorem. Promotion additionally requires the public adjacent-orbit interface and suffix persistence; a finite wall table or an infinite subsequence alone does not close that interface.
